verdict.rationale: RustDesk lets users decide where their connection infrastructure and data live by self-hosting the ID/rendezvous and relay servers on their own infrastructure. Clients connect peer to peer and fall back to the user's own relay, and the vendor says self-hosting keeps data fully under the user's control. Residency is achieved only by running your own servers: there is no documented region or residency selection for RustDesk's own hosted servers, and community reports raise uncertainty about where the default public relays are located. missing for 10: a documented region/residency choice for vendor-hosted servers, explicit documentation of where data is processed or stored, independent corroboration of residency guarantees.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Server OSS: a free, open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you can deploy on your own infrastructure.
self-hosted RustDesk keeps your data fully under your control.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, set up your own, or write your own rendezvous/relay server.
clients connect peer to peer when they can and fall back to your relay.
